correct_answer: The $218K belongs in the FY25 G&A base under TCI (Rev 6) because it was incurred in December; the compliance risk is the missing PM sign-off, which doesn't affect CAS treatment but creates a FAR 31.201-2(d) adequacy question for DCAA.
rationale: The December delivery receipt establishes the incurred date per CAS 9904.401 (consistency in estimating, accumulating, and reporting costs). Linda's own guidance in the Teams thread confirms that incurred date — not posting date — determines which fiscal year and which CAS revision applies. Since it was incurred in FY25, Rev 6 (TCI) governs, and the $218K belongs in the FY25 G&A allocation base. The compliance risk is real but distinct from the CAS question: the journal entry was auto-approved by a cost analyst without PM authorization. Under FAR 31.201-2(d), costs must be adequately documented. The missing PM sign-off doesn't make the cost unallowable per se, but gives DCAA grounds to question the adequacy of internal controls. Answer A incorrectly applies posting date rather than incurred date and applies the wrong CAS revision. Answer C overstates the consequence of missing PM approval — cost suspension is not required merely because a PM was on PTO; the delivery receipt and invoice substantiate the cost. Answer D conflates Rev 6 and Rev 7 methodologies — the VACI $100K exclusion only applies to costs governed by Rev 7 (FY26 forward), not retroactively to FY25 costs.
